sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "Building character, enriching lives, and having fun describe our **Trinity Extended Day
> (TED)** program. While providing a vital service for many families, TED offers a safe,
> well-structured environment for every Trinity student."

> "Extended Day provides an opportunity and space for students to focus on academics
> through **dedicated homework time** and to learn how to navigate social relationships.
> This is accomplished through group projects and fun-focused activities, all aimed at
> extending the Wildcat learning experience."

> "Students participate in various activities such as art, board games, **Fun Friday
> activities**, etc. Students are expected to adhere to the **Trinity Honor Code** while
> participating in Extended Day."

sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "Extended Day **begins at dismissal time** and continues until **6 pm**."

> ⚠️ **The page does NOT state the school day as 8:00 am–3:00 pm.** It says "begins at
> dismissal time". **The 8–3 school day is not found on this page** — do not attribute it
> here.

The rate card does independently establish **8:00am–5:30pm** on full days (when school is
closed but TED runs) and **"early dismissal–5:30pm"** on half days.

sections.text:
**TED is afternoon-only on regular school days.** Grepping the page for
`morning care|before care|before-care|before school|drop off` returns **0 hits**. The only
`8:00am` on the rate card belongs to the **full-day** rate, i.e. days when school is
closed.

**This is a confident null, not an oversight** — and there is positive evidence for that
reading: the school's **summer camp explicitly sells before-care at $85/week**. Trinity
clearly knows how to offer and price morning care; it simply does not during the school
year.

sections.text:
From the Cost of Attendance doc, section "Trinity Extended Day Fees - TED":

| Household income | Estimated TED Monthly Cost |
|---|---|
| Less than $30,000 | **$105** |
| $30,000 – $60,000 | **$135** |
| $60,000 – $90,000 | **$195** |
| Over $90,000 | **$380** (`$355`-sibling) |

> ⚠️ **The column header is the school's own: "ESTIMATED TED Monthly Cost."** The school
> hedges this figure itself.

**Per-day rates, all verbatim:**

> "**Drop-In Rate: $31/day** or **$25/day** for families receiving financial support.
> *TED is open until 6pm on regular school days.*"

> "**Full Day Rate: $72/day** or **$45/day for first child ($40-sibling)** for families
> receiving financial support. *TES is closed, but TED is open from **8:00am-5:30pm**.*"

> "**Half Day Rate: Complimentary to TED Monthly attendees. $51/day** or **$30/day** for
> families receiving financial support. *TED is open from **early dismissal-5:30pm**.*"

**This is an unusually good affordability story**: income-scaled monthly rates **and** a
reduced rate on every single drop-in tier, plus half days free to monthly attendees.

sections.text:
An earlier sweep recorded these; **none of them could be located**:

| Claimed policy | Status |
|---|---|
| Billing averaged over **"18.5 days/month × 10 months"** | **NOT FOUND** — 0 hits for `18.5`, `averag`, `10 month` across the TED page and the cost doc |
| **1.5% late fee** after 14 days | **NOT FOUND** — 0 hits |
| **Three occasions → removal** from TED | **NOT FOUND** — no TED late-pickup policy is published at all |

### ⚠️ CONSEQUENCE: no annual TED figure is defensible

Without a published billing basis — and with the school labelling its own monthly figure
"Estimated" — **an annual cost cannot be derived and must not be published.**
**Report TED as a monthly rate.**

> These are **not found**, not confirmed-absent. They read like real policy language and
> plausibly live in the TED registration form or a handbook, neither of which was opened.
> **Do not record them as verified nulls.**

**For contrast, the summer camp's late-pickup rule IS published**, and it is **two**
instances, not three — and it is both monetary and removal:
> "There is a **five-minute grace period** at pick-up time. After 12:05 (half-day), 4:05
> (full-day) and 5:35 (after-camp care), there will be a **$5/minute charge**. **Two or
> more instances of late pick up in one week could result in non-refunded removal from
> the program.**"

**Do not transfer the camp's rule to TED.** They are different programmes.

sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "TED also offers **enrichment programs, for an additional fee**, several days a week.
> These are led by a combination of Trinity faculty/staff and independent contractors.
> Examples of enrichments include **chess club, music lessons, karate, cheer club** and
> more."

**A confirmed null on pricing** — the page explicitly says "for an additional fee" and
**never states one**.

> ⚠️ "**Examples of** … **and more**" means this is **not an exhaustive list**. Do not
> present these four as the complete enrichment roster.

sections.subtopic: ⚠️ "Enrichments" is overloaded at Trinity — do not cross-wire
sections.preview: The Lower/Middle School "Enrichments" pages are curricular subjects (art, PE, Spanish, music, STEM lab) — free, under Academics. TED's "enrichments" are paid after-school add-ons. They are different things sharing a word.
sections.text:
The **Lower/Middle School "Enrichments" pages** are **curricular subjects** (art, PE,
Spanish, music, STEM lab) — free, under Academics. **TED's "enrichments" are paid
after-school add-ons.** They are different things sharing a word.
